title: Normalized compact-support projection descent maps
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and the normalized reduction presentations $r_T$ and total limits $L_T$ on integral modules and strict coefficient systems [def-sp-projection-reduction-presentation], with normalized reconstruction adjunctions [det-sp-normalized-equivalence]. A descent model consists of the prescribed integral tensor and open projection presentations [def-pur-integral-ringed-projection-maps], system tensor presentations and pullback comparisons for the varying-ring operations $G,P,J$ [def-sp-varying-ring-operations], together with tensor/scalar and pullback/scalar isomorphisms. The tensor comparisons are normalized on whole flat-term K-flat quotient complexes as in the reduction presentation. The pullback comparisons send each ordinary quotient augmentation of the geometric pullback unit to the system pullback unit; their derived maps are induced by the same strict-complex squares. The system tensor pullback is normalized by its ordinary unit tensor sections. The inverse open scalar comparison is exactly the mate of the pullback/scalar map under the two open adjunctions. These are presentations and normalization conditions, not existence assertions.

For a compactification $c=(j,p)$ of $f$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements], define $F_R=Rp_*j_!$ and $F_\bullet=PJ$. Proper scalar exchange $h:r_YRp_*\to P r_Z$ is the mate of the inverse pullback/scalar comparison. Define open/limit and proper/limit maps by transposing $d\,J(\epsilon)$ and $h\,P(\epsilon)$ under $r\dashv L$, respectively. Define $\alpha_N$ as $F_R(\eta_N)$ followed by these open/limit and proper/limit maps, and define reconstruction $b_N=\epsilon\,r_Y(\alpha_N)$. For $H=M\otimes f^*K$, define the system projection as the proper counit tensor mate followed by the proper image of the inverse open unit tensor mate, using the canonical pullback compositor. When the stated reconstruction maps and open inverse are invertible, the source coordinate is $\mu_{F_RM,K}$ followed by $b_M\otimes1$, the target coordinate is $b_H$ followed by $F_\bullet$ of the tensor/scalar and pullback/scalar maps, and the transported projection is source coordinate, system projection, inverse target coordinate. All maps retain the actual units, counits and quotient transitions.
